claims.text: The starting material is a nominally equiatomic W-Ta-V-Ti refractory high-entropy alloy.
The as-cast precursor has a single-BCC, directionally solidified dendrite-interdendrite structure.
The precursor contains approximately 71 vol.% W/Ta-rich dendrites and 29 vol.% Ti/V-rich interdendritic channels.
Immersion in molten Cu at 1200 °C for 96 h will selectively extract Ti and create a directionally aligned bicontinuous composite.
The resulting composite will contain approximately 63.6 vol.% BCC RHEA ligaments and 36.4 vol.% nearly pure FCC Cu channels.
Each RHEA/Cu interface will be coated by an approximately 300 nm W-rich interlayer.
Minor HCP Ti-rich precipitates will form behind the W-rich interlayer.
Ti preferentially dissolves from the interdendritic regions into molten Cu because Ti and Cu have a negative heat of mixing.
Selective Ti dissolution leaves W, Ta, and V behind as stable RHEA ligaments.
Continued Ti extraction causes W to accumulate at the RHEA/Cu interface because W has a strongly positive heat of mixing with Cu.
The W-rich interlayer passivates and stabilizes the RHEA/Cu interface.
The W-rich interlayer enhances bonding between the RHEA and Cu constituents.
Directionally aligned Cu channels provide effective thermal-conduction pathways.
The compositionally complex RHEA network impedes defect migration and blister formation, thereby reducing He-induced swelling.

The dealloyed composite will have significantly greater high-temperature thermal conductivity than the unprocessed WTaVTi precursor and conventional W-Cu composites, especially above approximately 650 °C.
The dealloyed composite will exhibit reduced He-induced swelling relative to the unprocessed alloy and conventional W-Cu composites.
Blistering in the dealloyed composite will be delayed relative to pure W under 25 keV He+ irradiation.
The expected irradiation benefit is based on 25 keV He+ screening of precursor dendrites rather than testing under neutron irradiation or long-term fusion service.
The RHEA framework is mechanically robust and contributes to durability of the composite.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis attributes reduced He-induced swelling to the dealloyed RHEA-Cu composite and proposes irradiating that composite, but the boundary states that the claimed irradiation benefit is based on screening precursor dendrites. The evidentiary object therefore differs from the material for which the irradiation outcome is predicted.
